points.event: Aug 20: ~14,800 excess deaths in France Aug 1-20; no excess in the last third of August

events.event: heat wave begins (Aug 2); max temperatures 11-12 C above seasonal norm for 9 consecutive days (s1)
Aug 12: national daily-mean temperature peak 28.6 C; daily excess deaths above 1,000 on Aug 12 and 13

threat.notes: extent = share of the ~14,800 French excess deaths (Aug 1-20) that had occurred. No sourced daily series was retrieved, so only endpoints are given; the sourced shape is: deaths rose with temperature, peaked Aug 12-13 (>1,000 excess per day), and stopped by Aug 20. Europe-wide the summer toll exceeded 70,000 (s3). If you need an intermediate curve, follow the temperature shape and label it as such, or fetch the daily series from s1 (figure 1) later.

fragments.notes: heat was forecast; no heat-HEALTH warning system existed to route it
existence of earlier systems not confirmed in this pass; date approximate

fragments.had: the first signal that thousands were dying
fragments.notes: public alarm around Aug 10-11; day not confirmed
activated Aug 13, after the mortality peak

fragments.had: national heat plan with health alert system

aggregation.notes: Derived from documented response dates (days after Aug 1, 2003), not a measured distribution: p10 ~ ER doctors' public alarm (~Aug 10-11, day unverified, s7), median = Plan Blanc Aug 13 (t=12, s4), p90 = national heat plan June 1 2004 (t=305, s6). Very skewed: the emergency response came after the peak; the lasting fix took ten months.

deploy.notes: Time until a standing heat-health warning plan existed (June 1, 2004).

ai_counterfactual.basis: Illustrative. The fragments were a forecast (available at the start) plus health signals (ER admissions, funeral-home load) that humans connected ~9-12 days in. Joining a temperature forecast with a known heat-mortality relationship and routing a warning to hospitals and home-care services is a short expert analysis task, inside the ~17.4 h 50% task horizon in RATES.md (METR entry). Assumed: warning routed by day 3 (Aug 4), i.e. before the Aug 12-13 peak, with humans still deciding to activate plans. Not a claim that deaths would have been prevented; heat plans reduce but do not eliminate heat mortality.
ai_counterfactual.label: illustrative

gap_summary: ~14,800 excess deaths accumulated in 19 days, peaking on days 11-12; the hospital emergency plan came on day 12, after the peak, and the standing fix on day 305.
